sentences.text: Lactobacillus crispatus is prevalent and beneficial in the healthy human cervicovaginal microbiota, where vaginal lactobacilli are described as the first line of defence of the urogenital tract.
It produces copious amounts of lactic acid, which acts as a broad spectrum bactericide, virucide and immunomodulator.
In a citizen-science survey of 3,345 Belgian women, the taxon module containing it was positively linked to oestrogen levels and contraceptive use, and negatively to childbirth and breastfeeding.
Reviews report that dominance by this species in pregnancy is associated with lower risk of preterm delivery, and a strain has been trialled as a vaginal probiotic in bacterial vaginosis.
